prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 1997 – summary (under 500 words)

Vision and approach
- New Labour offers a modern, pragmatic centre-left “what counts is what works” programme for national renewal: for the many, not the few; ending old left/right dogmas; rebuilding trust through specific, measurable pledges.
- Ten core commitments: prioritize education; no rise in basic/top income tax; economic stability with low inflation; 250,000 young unemployed into work; rebuild the NHS and cut bureaucracy; be tough on crime and its causes (including halving juvenile case times); strengthen families and modernize welfare; safeguard the environment with integrated transport; clean up politics and decentralize power; lead and reform in Europe.

Economy, tax and work
- Stability first: tight inflation target; reform Bank of England for credible, depoliticized monetary policy; “golden rule” (borrow only to invest); stick to existing spending totals for 2 years; save to invest.
- No increase in basic/top income tax rates; long‑term goal of a 10p starting rate; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; fair, pro‑work tax/benefit reform.
- Fund a welfare‑to‑work programme via a one‑off windfall levy on privatized utilities.
- Back business: tougher competition law; fix and focus the Private Finance Initiative; Regional Development Agencies; support small firms (cut red tape, tackle late payment); science/technology and green industries push.
- Modern labour market: sensibly set National Minimum Wage via Low Pay Commission; union recognition where workers vote for it; support EU Social Chapter focused on employability.

Education and skills (number one priority)
- Cut infant class sizes to 30 or under by ending assisted places; universal nursery places for 4‑year‑olds.
- Drive up standards: literacy/numeracy targets, setting by ability, “fresh start” for failing schools; Education Action Zones; ICT National Grid for Learning; wire schools free.
- Support and accountability: General Teaching Council; tougher teacher training/induction; stronger heads.
- Lifelong learning: University for Industry; Individual Learning Accounts; income‑related graduate repayments.

Welfare to work and families
- 250,000 under‑25s off benefit into real jobs/training/education; help long‑term unemployed; tailored “Employment Zones”; clamp down on fraud.
- National childcare strategy; basic rights on working time, holidays, unpaid parental leave; retain and uprate Child Benefit.

NHS and public health
- End the internal market; shift money from admin to care; treat 100,000 extra patients as a first step; end waits for cancer surgery.
- Primary care‑led commissioning in groups; multi‑year service agreements; measure outcomes; raise NHS spending in real terms annually.
- Ban tobacco advertising; independent Food Standards Agency; promote telemedicine.

Crime and justice
- Tough on crime and causes: halve time from arrest to sentencing for persistent young offenders; final warning system; Youth Offender Teams.
- Decentralize CPS; sentencing guidelines and transparency; tackle disorder, stalking, domestic violence; new offences for racial harassment; anti‑drugs coordinator; free vote to ban all handguns; better support for victims.

Housing, pensions, care
- Help homeowners (consumer protection, tackle gazumping); reinvest council house receipts to build/repair homes; license HMOs; introduce commonhold; restore duty to house priority homeless.
- Retain basic state pension (price‑linked); promote secure second “stakeholder” pensions; retain SERPS option; carers’ rights; Royal Commission on long‑term care.

Environment, transport, rural, culture
- Every department “green”; integrated transport: stronger rail regulation and a new rail authority; public/private partnership for London Underground; roads review; cleaner vehicles; protect rural services and the Post Office; reform CAP; wider countryside access and wildlife protection.
- Arts/sport: create NESTA for young talent; protect school playing fields; back England’s 2006 World Cup bid; reform the Lottery with a not‑for‑profit operator.

Clean politics and constitution
- End hereditary peers’ voting rights; transparent party funding, ban foreign donations; Freedom of Information Act; incorporate the ECHR.
- Devolution by referendum: Scottish Parliament; Welsh Assembly; London mayor/strategic authority; regional chambers and possible elected assemblies; modernize Commons; empower and make local government accountable (best value).

Europe, foreign policy, defence, development
- Lead EU reform (single market, enlargement, CAP/CFP change, openness); sign Social Chapter; EMU decision by economic test and referendum.
- Defence rooted in NATO; strategic review; retain Trident; pursue arms control and ban landmines; UN and Commonwealth reform and engagement; new International Development department, move toward UN 0.7% aid target; human rights and ICC; cut CO2 by 20% by 2010.

Five election pledges
- Smaller infant classes; fast‑track persistent young offenders; cut NHS waiting lists (100,000 extra treated via £100m from red tape); 250,000 under‑25s into work (funded by windfall levy); no rise in income tax rates, cut VAT on heating to 5%, keep inflation/interest rates low.
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<what in the text informed your choice>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "party": one of ['Labour', 'Conservative', 'Liberal Democrats', 'Referendum Party', 'Scottish National Party']
}
